author: Sylvia Hughes
title: God is full of grace and mercy - NewsBreak
text: Grace, mercy, and peace will be with you from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love. - 2 John 3:6 Many years ago, when living in Virginia, I was supposed to pick up Thad Sr. when he got off work at 5 o’clock. Somehow I let time get away from me and when I looked at the clock it was close to time for me to be there. It took about 20 minutes to get to his workplace. For most of the way, it was just pure country, very few houses and those were set well back off the road. The road into town was four lanes and straight going. I hopped in the car and barreled down the road. About five miles into my journey, I noticed a light flashing in the rear window of my car. Oh boy! I just knew this was going to be bad. My speeding had got me in trouble and to top it off, I was now going to be later than ever. I pulled over and waited in dread for the patrolman to come to my window. When he got there, he said, “Do you know how fast you were going?” Why do they always ask that? Do they expect you to say, “Yes sir, I was going 90 in a fifty five?” I said, “I know I was speeding.” He proceeded to tell me what speed I was going and that he had followed me with the light on for a pretty good distance. “Where in the world were you going in such a hurry?” I explained it to him. That kind man scolded me and said he only wanted me to arrive safely at my destination. He asked me to please slow down and drive responsibly. He never spoke in anger or in a harsh manner. His voice was soft and gentle and he didn’t write me a ticket. Do you know what that was? That was grace and mercy. Grace because he gave me kindness when it was not deserved and mercy because he did not give me the punishment I certainly deserved. He could have written a ticket that caused me to lose my license for a long time, but he didn’t. He gave me a chance to change the way I was behaving. He asked me to consider that I would like to reach my destination safely. All of his actions on that day were an example of what God does for us and what He requires of those who follow Him. God gives grace and mercy to us every minute of the day. He requires that we show the same grace and mercy to others that we have received from Him. It isn’t easy for us humans. At least, it isn’t for me. I often fail, feel guilty, repent and hope to do better. God, who is full of grace and mercy, picks me up, sets me on my feet and urges me to rely more on His Spirit to guide me, show me what to do, what to say and not rely on my own frail self.
